Why trust a free tool with this?
Your documents and files are scanned entirely in your browser and never uploaded anywhere. No account, no ads, no catch - built by SafeNetwork from official gov.uk, IRCC, EU, and South African DHA guidance.
Does this predict approval?
No. This is guidance, not immigration advice - it checks how ready your documents and evidence look, not your chances of approval. Only the consulate or embassy decides that.
Which countries?
UK Standard Visitor, Canada visitor (TRV), Schengen short-stay (Type C), and South Africa visitor visas are all live. United States, Australia, and China are coming soon.

    Two documents make this a smooth ride

    Almost every applicant needs these two - get a head start now. The rest depends on your situation, covered next.

    🛂
    Your international passport
    Valid 6+ months past your return date.
    Why?
    If yours has expired or is close to it, renewing it is usually the slowest step in this whole process - start that first.
    🏦
    3-6 months of bank statements
    Downloaded from your banking app, not screenshots.
    Why?
    If you're pulling from more than one account, give yourself extra time - this consistently takes longer than people plan for.

    🌍 Travel Experience

    ▸
    Why?
    Just for your own planning - this doesn't affect your checklist and doesn't block anything here. A first-time Schengen applicant is typically granted a single-entry visa valid for around 10-15 days, covering the specific trip applied for, rather than a longer multiple-entry visa - that tends to come with a stronger travel history on later applications.
    Worth considering: a UK visa instead
    If the money for this trip isn't ready yet, it may be worth considering an application for the United Kingdom instead of a Schengen/European country. The UK typically grants a minimum of 6 months' validity, with multiple entry - which suits someone who doesn't have funds ready to travel right away - unlike a first-time Schengen visa, which is typically single-entry and only valid for around 10-15 days.
    This is general guidance, not a guarantee - actual visa validity and entry conditions are decided case-by-case by the consulate or entry clearance officer, and can differ from what's typical. You're free to continue with your European application either way - nothing here is required or blocks you from proceeding.

    No travel history yet - that's fine, plenty of successful applicants start here.

    Having visited an African country before is genuinely useful travel history for a UK/Schengen application. These five are commonly picked because they're straightforward for Nigerians to visit - tap one to see exactly what's involved.

    Entry tickets, tours, attractions - e.g. London Eye, museums, day trips.

Tick whichever you plan to visit; approximate adult ticket prices as of August 2026 (always confirm current prices on the attraction's own site before you travel). Free major museums are included too - visiting some of these alongside paid attractions is completely normal and doesn't weaken your case.

    ℹ️ Why the 2× buffer matters, beyond a checkbox

    This 2× figure is our own rule of thumb, not an official one. But a common concern behind visitor visa refusals is financial credibility - does your account show enough cushion that the trip wouldn't leave you unable to support yourself, or make it look like you're leaning on this trip in a way that puts your return home in doubt? Aiming for roughly double your trip cost is one simple way to build in that cushion. Falling short of it isn't automatic refusal - it just means it may be worth explaining your financial picture directly, for example in a cover letter, rather than leaving a gap for a reviewer to guess about.

    Ticking this makes the documents below required, and they need to come from your host - not something you can produce yourself. Reach out to them for these as early as possible:
    • Invitation letter from your UK host
    • Copy of host's status document (passport / residency proof / visa)
    • Host's proof of address (recent utility bill)
    • Host's bank statement or employment letter

    No rush - message them now, then carry on with the rest of the checklist below while you wait. Your progress here is saved automatically, so there's nothing to lose by coming back to this section once you have what you need.

    Not staying with a host? You'll need a hotel/accommodation booking confirmation instead - see below.
    Why?
    Being upfront about a past refusal - with a clear explanation of what's changed since - reads far better to a reviewer than a refusal they discover independently. Attach the refusal letter(s) under "Previous visa refusal documentation" below.

    🎓 Funded opportunities & exchange programs

    Can't yet afford the trip you're preparing for above? These are real, currently-running programs - scholarships, exchanges, and fellowships - that cover some or all of the cost for students in Nigeria. This list is separate from the visa checklist above; it isn't visa-specific, and Smooth Application isn't affiliated with any program on it.

    ⚠️ Watch for scams. A genuine scholarship, exchange, or fellowship never asks you to pay to be selected, to release your winnings, or to "process" your visa through them. Apply only through the official link shown for each program below - never through an agent, a WhatsApp/Telegram group, or a lookalike site that contacts you first. If in doubt, search the program's name plus the word "scam" before you pay anything or share your documents.

    Details above (funding, eligibility, deadlines) change year to year - always confirm the current cycle on the program's own official site before relying on anything here. Last checked: .

      🚫 Documents best avoided as sole evidence

      ▸

      Caseworkers across most visa systems give little weight to these on their own - use them only alongside stronger evidence above: credit card statements (not bank statements), driving licence as identity proof, flight/hotel bookings alone as proof of ties, photocopies where an original is reasonably available, and leisure or short-course certificates unrelated to your visit purpose.
